answer: Whether drones wander through an oceanic gale or verify a saffron harvest, each node must prove its identity via hardware-rooted attestation. Before transacting, an agent presents a cryptographic quote signed by a physical secure enclave. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of purchasing discrete silicon chips per identity, preventing arbitrary software replication. However, this model centralizes trust in semiconductor foundries and remains vulnerable to side-channel key extraction.
